material_premises.fact: The registry defines 15 PUBLIC_FIXED_BAR predicates; all 15 have score_producing_route_ready=false in the readiness matrix.

Source review classifies 8 of the 15 as owner-computed or owner-private (no third-party route to an official score), 3 as third-party runnable in principle (TB4, TB-Science, LiveBench IF), and 4 as unresolved (HLE, Chartography, OSWorld 2.1, and AutomationBench whose bar comes from the private official set). Per-predicate rows with excerpts are in public_bar_rows.

The bars come from a mix of evaluators: Anthropic's own runs at max (TB4: xhigh) effort (TB4, TB-Science, HLE with tools, OSWorld, Chartography) and benchmark-owner measurements (Artificial Analysis: AA-Briefcase, GDPval-AA, Finance & Accounting Index; Vals: Finance Agent v2, MysteryMechanism; Zapier: AutomationBench; Cursor: CursorBench; Cognition: FrontierCode). Independent-harness measurements can differ materially (HLE: 67.7% with Anthropic's tools vs 61.4% on Artificial Analysis's harness). 'Comparable harness' therefore means reproducing the evaluator's setup, which for several surfaces includes paid frontier LLM graders or judges.

No pinned donor-independent response generator or agent adapter is bound anywhere in the readiness matrix: AutomationBench lacks 'a frozen donor-independent OpenAI-compatible or equivalent Brain endpoint', LiveBench IF is 'SCORER_READY__GENERATOR_MISSING', Terminal-Bench-Science has 'no bound general Brain agent adapter'. Earlier Brain routes with local Qwen3.5 4B/9B and a Pollinations non-frontier planner were falsified. A pinned open-weights route does exist on Cloudflare Workers AI but its $0 allocation is far below benchmark scale (see 2026-10-02_ZERO_COST_SUBSTRATE_ROUTE_CENSUS_V1).
Free unlimited GitHub-hosted runners (public repositories) are Linux 4 vCPU / 16 GB RAM / 14 GB SSD, x64 or arm64; the standard table lists no GPU runner.

The highest-scoring open model that fits in 12 GB at 4-bit (Qwen3.5 9B) scores 9.2% on Terminal-Bench (Epoch data through Apr 2026; benchmark version unspecified), about 57 points below the 66.4% bar.

On Artificial Analysis's Terminal-Bench 4.0 board (mini-SWE-agent harness) the best open-weights model scores 41.8% (GLM-5.3, #9) against a 70.6% leader; Kimi K3 scores 12.6 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro 14.6 on the same board. Near-frontier open-weights models are 744B-1.6T-parameter MoEs 'realistically deployable only on rented H100s, Mac Ultras, or standard inference nodes', i.e. not on a free CPU carrier. Vendor-reported figures on custom harnesses are higher but unpinned.

On Cognition's own FrontierCode 1.1 Main leaderboard the best open-weights rows are Kimi K3 at 44.2% and GLM 5.3 (max) at 40.1%, against Opus 5.5 (medium) at 54.6% - a gap of about 10 points, far smaller than on Terminal-Bench 4.0 (P7). Open-weights status of those models is from secondary reports.

The project's own frozen route audit reports zero_cost_executable_surface_count = 0 and portfolio_prequalification_pass_count = 0 across 14 surfaces, with five private surfaces already deleted as execution routes and the rule that 'PRIVATE_OR_GATED_OFFICIAL_SURFACES_MUST_BE_REPLACED_BY_SCOPE_EQUIVALENT_ABSOLUTE_PROOF_OR_REMAIN_BLOCKED'.

relation_to_prior_work.detail: The owner's frozen audit already finds zero zero-cost-executable surfaces among 14 (P9). This receipt adds a quantified substrate ceiling (P5-P8) and primary-source reasons for each surface's classification.

Same operational conclusion for FrontierCode, CursorBench, AA-Briefcase, Finance Agent v2 and MysteryMechanism: they cannot be execution routes. This receipt supplies official primary-source evidence of why (owner-run private tasks, probes and Elo).

That candidate keeps the six affected predicates frozen and requires independent scope-complete stronger proofs that imply each unchanged bar; its own nonclaims say behavioral obligation coverage does not establish numeric bar equivalence. No discharge mechanism is visible in the repo. INFERENCE: a numeric bar on a private, unobservable population cannot be implied by finite Brain-side evidence without scope transport, which the project already forbids (OPUS55_SYNTHESIS_ZERO_REALITY_DISCHARGE_EXHAUSTION_V1: finite_empirical_scope_transport = INDEPENDENTLY_FORBIDDEN). Testable by the first BUILD_*_STRONGER_PROOF attempt; the repo's own fallback is 'remain blocked'.

It lists BIND_GDPVAL_PUBLIC_ROUTE and BIND_FINANCE_ACCOUNTING_INDEX_PUBLIC_ROUTE as live public route candidates. Primary sources show the scored quantities (GDPval-AA Elo, Finance & Accounting Index) are Artificial Analysis computations (judge-panel pairwise Elo anchored to AA's model pool; a composite that includes the private AA-Briefcase), so the numeric bars are not third-party reproducible although GDPval's task data is public. The same deletion logic would apply unless a precise public surrogate with a scope audit is adopted.

The frozen public-600 binding, and the AutomationBench Brain gateway in open PR 865 (operative configuration; substrate not yet qualified), are untouched by this finding. The question raised is whether the 40.0 bar, taken from the private official set, may be applied to the public set at all.

conclusion: No unilateral zero-cost route to the conjunction of the 15 public-bar predicates is currently evidenced, and the project's own route audit agrees (zero_cost_executable_surface_count = 0 of 14 surfaces). Eight predicates are owner-computed or owner-private: the project cannot measure them, and the only candidate route is the owner's stronger-proof substitution, for which no discharge mechanism is visible and which, by the project's own scope-transport prohibition, cannot imply a numeric bar on an unobservable private population from finite Brain-side evidence (an inference to be tested by the first BUILD_*_STRONGER_PROOF attempt; the repo's fallback for such predicates is to remain blocked). Three predicates are third-party runnable (TB4, TB-Science, LiveBench IF) but all need a pinned donor-independent generator that is not bound in the repo (a pinned open-weights route exists on Cloudflare Workers AI, but its $0 allocation is orders of magnitude below one benchmark pass; see 2026-10-02_ZERO_COST_SUBSTRATE_ROUTE_CENSUS_V1): the best CPU-hostable open model found scores 9.2% on Terminal-Bench (version unspecified), about 57 points below the TB4 bar, and the best open-weights model on an independent TB4 board (41.8%) needs GPU-class inference that is not zero-cost. Because the terminal certificate requires every predicate, the terminal goal cannot be made true by capability work inside the current constraints unless the owner-computed predicates are re-posed or proven by a mechanism not yet shown, and a pinned generator is bound. This is evidence about the formulation and constraints, not a claim that Opus-level capability is impossible in principle. CORRECTION (added later in this PR): LiveBench Instruction Following is an exception to the generator and capability gap described for agentic surfaces; open-weights models already exceed its bar (census P13), making it the first credible zero-cost route to a real predicate. AUTOMATIONBENCH_GE_40 is reclassified as UNRESOLVED: its surface is public but its bar comes from the private official set, so passing it would not be scope-equivalent to Opus 5.5 (defect_findings). SECOND CORRECTION: for LIVEBENCH_IF_GE_65_7 the repo's declared metric (prompt-level loose accuracy) differs from the leaderboard's (strict, mean of prompt-level and instruction-level) and the registry's release label matches no LiveBench release; the route stays the shortest path only if the owner pipeline fixes the metric and shows the question-set match (defect_findings).

upstream_robustness_findings: nltk.download('stopwords') is called inside functions on every stop-word check and punkt at import: a scoring run is network-dependent unless nltk.download is made a local-presence check (done in the driver, fail closed).
upstream's exception handler indexes turns[0].split('<instructions>')[1] and crashes on prompts without those tags: the driver scores such a question 0 and reports it.
